prompt: Tangent is defined as $\tan\theta = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$. At $45^\circ$ the sine and the cosine are exactly equal. What is $\tan 45^\circ$?
hint: The sine and cosine are the same number at $45^\circ$, so you are dividing a number by ITSELF.

hints.text: The sine and cosine are the same number at $45^\circ$, so you are dividing a number by ITSELF.
Any number that is not zero, divided by itself, gives the same result every time. Apply that to $\frac{\sin 45^\circ}{\cos 45^\circ}$.
A number divided by itself is $1$, so $\tan 45^\circ = 1$.

explanation: The tangent is sine divided by cosine, which is height up divided by distance across.
At $45^\circ$ the point is exactly on the diagonal, so it is as far up as it is across: $\sin 45^\circ = \cos 45^\circ$.
Dividing two equal nonzero numbers gives $1$, so $\tan 45^\circ = 1$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Use the actual values
steps: 0.707 ÷ 0.707 = 1. The messy square roots cancel each other out.

alternativeExplanations.title: Tangent is slope
steps: tan θ is rise over run — the steepness of the line from the centre out to the point.
At 45° the line rises 1 for every 1 it runs, which is a slope of exactly 1.
